thread:
finn: Quick heads-up  I opened a small PR to align the Ruby SDK's retry behavior with the Go SDK (backoff and idempotency checks). Noticed a handful of onboarding runs where the Ruby sampleapp gives up on token-refresh transient 502s faster than Go. Can someone from SDK team weigh in?

anika: Can you paste the failure pattern? Is it a 502 vs 503 or connection reset?

finn: Mostly 502 Bad Gateway right after token rotate while we hit the auth proxy during CI stress. Repro locally by running the sampleapp and hammering refresh endpoint with `ab -n 50 -c 10` after rotating tokens. Ruby client retries twice with fixed 100ms, then gives up. Go client does exponential backoff (100, 200, 400ms) and succeeds most of the time.

ram: Looks like we never implemented exponential backoff in the Ruby helper. PR (link in description) adds a small backoff util but I worry about parity: Go also treats POSTs to /generate as non-idempotent and doesn't retry body-changing requests. We should mirror that in Ruby.

anika: Yes we should match semantics. Two things: 1) same default backoff schedule, 2) same idempotency heuristics (retry safe if method is GET or has idempotency-key header). Also add an env var to opt into aggressive retries for dev (SAMPLEAPP_RETRY_DEV=true) so onboarding tests are more stable.

finn: Proposed quick change: in sdk/core/retry.rb implement exponential_backoff(base: 100, factor: 2, max_retries: 3) and wire sampleapp to use it for token-refresh only. Add unit that asserts sleep calls (mocked) to avoid flakiness in tests.

ram: small nit: tests should assert we don't retry on 401 (auth error). Only 5xx and network errors. Also add a flaky-integration that simulates intermittent 502 to confirm sampleapp recovers.

anika: Agreed. Also add a short note in CHANGELOG about parity and bump minor version. We don't need a major bump since behavior is opt-in via config by default? Which default do we pick? Keep old behavior or flip to match Go out of the box?

finn: I'd prefer flipping to match Go by default (consistency across SDKs is valuable), but that could change failure modes for users. Maybe flip in minor and call out in the release notes and provide a compatibility env var to opt out (RUBY_SDK_LEGACY_RETRY=true).

ram: Sounds reasonable. For the PR: include migration notes, add integration smoke job `ruby-sdk-retry-parity-smoke` to CI matrix, and request a quick security review (since retries can change observable timing).

ci-bot: CI queued: ruby-sdk-unit #1212, ruby-sampleapp-integration #58.

maintainer-bot: Reminder: run `bundle update --bundler` before merging to avoid CI bundler mismatch.

anika: Thanks  if you push tests and CI passes I'm happy to approve. One more test request: include a token-rotation scenario where the retry honors idempotency-key header for POSTs so we don't accidentally retry non-idempotent calls.

finn: Will add tests + opt-out env var + integration smoke job. Pushing update now.
